rows.Finding description: A 5-minute fluorescent-ligand uptake assay in APOE4 versus isogenic APOE3 human iPSC-derived astrocytes showed less transferrin uptake and a trend toward fewer internalized EGF puncta (n=12 samples, 30–50 cells per sample), measuring early receptor-mediated internalization without measuring recycling rate or ARF6 activity.
rows.Finding quote: APOE4 astrocytes trend towards internalizing less EGF (Figure 1G,H). Using fluorescently-tagged Tf, we again observed that APOE4 astrocytes internalized less Tf than APOE3 astrocytes.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (less transferrin internalization and a trend toward fewer internalized EGF puncta in human iPSC-derived astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived, FACS-purified astrocytes from one isogenic APOE3/APOE4 pair generated from an APOE3-homozygous parental line; study parental donors were female. Early-passage cells (<P8); fluorescent EGF (100 ng/mL) or transferrin (25 µg/mL) uptake for 5 minutes at 37°C following cooling on ice, followed by washing, fixation and confocal microscopy; EGF puncta per cell and transferrin internalization per cell quantified.

rows.Finding description: Representative images after a 5-minute fluorescent EGF pulse showed a trend toward reduced EGF internalization in APOE4 compared with isogenic APOE3 human iPSC-derived astrocytes.
rows.Finding quote: APOE4 astrocytes trend towards internalizing less EGF (Figure 1G,H).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (trend toward reduced early EGF internalization in human iPSC-derived astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived astrocytes from one isogenic APOE3/APOE4 pair with an APOE3 homozygous parental line; early-passage cells (<P8). EGF conjugated to AlexaFluor555 (100 ng/mL) was applied for 5 minutes at 37°C, followed by washing, fixation and confocal fluorescence microscopy. ARF6 activity and receptor recycling were not measured.

rows.Finding description: Comparing isogenic human APOE4 and APOE3 iPSC-derived astrocytes revealed no significant difference in Rab11-positive recycling-endosome levels, which do not establish ARF6-related receptor recycling flux.
rows.Finding quote: In contrast to our finding in early endocytic effectors, we noted no difference in Rab11 (recycling endosome) levels between cells of the APOE3 and APOE4 genotype (Figure S2A,B).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in Rab11-positive recycling-endosome levels in human iPSC-derived astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived astrocytes comparing isogenic APOE3 and APOE4 genotypes; the study used two independent isogenic pairs derived from female Coriell AG09173 and AG10788 parental lines, with experiments performed at early passage (<P8). No additional treatment specified for this comparison. Results describes Rab11 immunofluorescence, but S2A/B are reported jointly without individual panel modalities or panel-specific line assignment.

rows.Finding description: Comparison of isogenic APOE4 and APOE3 human iPSC-derived astrocytes showed no significant difference in Rab11-positive recycling-endosome levels, a marker readout that does not establish receptor recycling flux or ARF6 involvement.
rows.Finding quote: In contrast to our finding in early endocytic effectors, we noted no difference in Rab11 (recycling endosome) levels between cells of the APOE3 and APOE4 genotype (Figure S2A,B).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in Rab11-positive recycling-endosome levels in human iPSC-derived astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived astrocytes from homozygous APOE3/APOE4 isogenic pairs; study parental lines were Coriell AG09173 and AG10788, both female. Experiments used early-passage astrocytes (<P8). Results describe Rab11 immunofluorescence to examine recycling endosomes and report S2A/B jointly; the specific parental background, assay modality, and measurement assigned to S2B cannot be established without the supplement.
rows.Data location: Supplementary Fig S2B (reported jointly with S2A in Results)

rows.Finding description: HPCD treatment versus PBS increased membrane-enriched ABCA1 and significantly decreased membrane-enriched caveolin-1 in APOE4-TR mouse cortex (10 mice per group, five females and five males), consistent with an indirect rescue of impaired trafficking.
rows.Finding quote: Brain tissue fractionation showed a significant decrease in total membrane caveolin-1 levels in HPCD treated-APOE4-TR mice, along with enhanced ABCA1 recycling, as indicated by increased membrane ABCA1 levels (Fig. 5 F).
rows.Finding summary: (PBS -> HPCD in APOE4-TR mice) -> (increased cortical membrane-enriched ABCA1 and decreased caveolin-1)
rows.Experimental system: Cortical tissue, without cell-type isolation, from male and female human APOE4 targeted-replacement mice purchased from JAX; treatment began at 8 months with subcutaneous HPCD (2 g/kg) or PBS twice weekly for eight weeks and continued during two weeks of behavioral testing; tissue fractionation and western blotting measured total membrane-enriched ABCA1 and caveolin-1.

rows.Finding description: Western blotting of isolated brain lysosomes from 14-month-old APOE3-TR and APOE4-TR mice (4–5 mice per group, mixed sexes) showed higher lysosomal ABCA1 protein levels in APOE4-TR mice.
rows.Finding quote: Lysosomes isolated from mouse brains showed higher ABCA1 protein levels in the lysosomal fractions of APOE4-TR mice (Fig. 4 J).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher ABCA1 protein levels in isolated brain lysosomes)
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE3- and APOE4-targeted-replacement mice purchased from JAX, 14 months old, mixed sexes; lysosomes isolated from bulk brain tissue using the Minute Lysosome Isolation Kit and ABCA1 measured by western blotting; no cell-type separation or experimental treatment reported for this comparison. ARF6 activity and receptor recycling were not directly measured.

rows.Finding description: HPTLC analysis of secreted cholesterol, cholesteryl esters (CE), and phosphatidylethanolamine (PE) in APOE-isogenic human iAstrocytes showed significantly lower cholesterol and CE secretion in APOE4 than APOE3, providing an indirect ABCA1-function surrogate.
rows.Finding quote: Interestingly, secreted cholesterol and CE were significantly decreased only in APOE4 iAstrocytes (Figures S2A and S2B).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower cholesterol and CE secretion in human iAstrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human quiescent iPSC-derived astrocytes from EBiSC CRISPR-generated APOE-isogenic lines BIONi010-C-2 (APOE3) and BIONi010-C-4 (APOE4), each expressing a single APOE allele; differentiated through neural progenitor cells using a 44-day astrocyte differentiation protocol; baseline without cytokine stimulation; secreted lipids measured by HPTLC and normalized to cellular phosphatidylcholine.

rows.Finding description: Across three independent experiments, flow cytometry showed a lower baseline Aβ42 uptake trend in APOE4 versus APOE3 human isogenic iAstrocytes with no significant difference (p = 0.054), while RAP significantly decreased uptake in APOE3 but caused no significant difference in APOE4 (p = 0.23).
rows.Finding quote: A flow-cytometry-based Aβ42 uptake assay, using pre-aggregated Hilyte488-tagged Aβ42, showed an allele-dependent trend in uptake capacity (KO > E2 > E3 ≥ E4), although differences between APOE3 and APOE4 did not reach significance (p = 0.054) (Figure 2F). Interestingly, APOE-KO cells showed the highest Aβ42 uptake capacity. Aβ42 is mostly taken up through receptor-dependent endocytosis, such as LRP1. To determine if Aβ uptake in iAstrocytes is mediated by LDLR-dependent endocytosis, we treated cells with a low concentration of LDLR family antagonist receptor-associated protein (RAP), which primarily blocked LRP1 and very-low-density lipoprotein receptor (VLDLR), in order to induce a mild reduction in Aβ uptake, resulting in a measurable difference between genotypes. Blocking LDLR family members caused a significant decrease in Aβ uptake in APOE-KO, E2, and E3, but not in E4 iAstrocytes (p = 0.23).
rows.Finding summary: Baseline uptake trended lower in APOE4 than APOE3 (p = 0.054). RAP significantly reduced uptake in APOE3. Its effect in APOE4 did not reach significance (p = 0.23). The paper gives no genotype-by-RAP interaction test.
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE-isogenic iAstrocytes assayed by flow cytometry for the percentage of live Aβ-positive cells using 1 μM pre-aggregated labeled Aβ42, with or without 24 h pretreatment with 0.2 μM RAP. The supplied text does not verify two-hour Aβ exposure or continued RAP during exposure.

rows.Finding description: Across three independent experiments comparing glutamate uptake over 1 hour in APOE-isogenic human iAstrocytes, APOE4 cells showed lower uptake than APOE3 and the lowest uptake overall, providing an indirect functional surrogate for transporter availability without measuring ARF6-related recycling.
rows.Finding quote: Uptake of glutamate in iAstrocytes demonstrated an allele-dependent effect, with APOE4 iAstrocytes taking up the lowest amount of glutamate while APOE2 and APOE-KO took up the highest amounts (Figure 2D).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower glutamate uptake in human iAstrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human monoallelic EBiSC APOE3 and APOE4 iAstrocytes differentiated through day 44 and plated 24 h before assay. Glutamate uptake over 1 h was normalized to total lysate protein. The supplied text does not specify glutamine deprivation, glutamate concentration, assay temperature, or detection reagent.
